name: bxe_init_locked
prose: Precondition: sc is a valid softc and the core lock is held (BXE_CORE_LOCK_ASSERT). Postcondition: returns 0 immediately if IFF_DRV_RUNNING is already set; returns ENXIO immediately, without touching IFF_DRV_RUNNING, if sc->state is BXE_STATE_ERROR and recovery_state is BXE_RECOVERY_FAILED. Otherwise it sets power state D0; for a PF with a pending reset or parity attention it may attempt leader recovery, and if that does not complete it moves the device to D3hot, sets recovery_state to BXE_RECOVERY_FAILED and goes to the common exit with rc = ENXIO. If no recovery failure occurs it sets recovery_state to BXE_RECOVERY_DONE and calls bxe_nic_load(sc, LOAD_OPEN), keeping its return code as rc. At the common exit any nonzero rc (ENXIO from the recovery failure, or whatever bxe_nic_load returned) is logged and IFF_DRV_RUNNING is cleared; rc is returned and the core lock stays held.
note: Both reviewer claims right: load failure returns bxe_nic_load's rc (bxe.c:12930-12941) and the early ENXIO return at 12874 skips the IFF_DRV_RUNNING clearing at 12938.

name: bxe_prev_unload_common
prose: Precondition: sc is a valid softc for a device whose path may have been left loaded by a previous function. Postcondition: if bxe_prev_is_path_marked(sc) is true it returns bxe_prev_mcp_done(sc) right away, with no MAC close, BRB drain or common reset (but bxe_prev_mcp_done itself runs). Otherwise it reads MISC_REG_RESET_REG_1; only if the RST_BRB1 bit is set does it close the MAC Rx paths and the LLH filters, check for UNDI (when RST_DORQ is set and DORQ_REG_NORM_CID_OFST reads 0x7, it clears that offset), and poll BRB1_REG_NUM_OF_FULL_BLOCKS until empty or until the timer runs out (logging "Failed to empty BRB" on timeout). Then in both remaining cases it calls bxe_reset_common, rewrites any saved xmac/umac/emac/bmac register values that were recorded, and calls bxe_prev_mark_path(sc, prev_undi); if that returns nonzero it calls bxe_prev_mcp_done(sc), ignores its result and returns the marking error; otherwise it returns bxe_prev_mcp_done(sc).
note: Reviewers right on both: MAC/UNDI/BRB steps are inside the RST_BRB1 test (bxe.c:15556-15609); already-marked path still calls bxe_prev_mcp_done (15549-15551). Lock claim in old prose removed (not checked). Function actually starts at 15531 (slice start 15331).

name: bxe_nic_unload
prose: Precondition: sc is a valid softc and the core lock is held (BXE_CORE_LOCK_ASSERT). It first clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING, zeroes each fastpath watchdog_timer and briefly takes and releases each fastpath TX lock, and for a PF with the shmem2 capability flag clears the LOADED_L2 bit. It then returns -1 (after logging an error) when sc is a PF whose recovery_state is not BXE_RECOVERY_DONE and whose state is BXE_STATE_CLOSED or BXE_STATE_ERROR; only in CHIP_4_PORT_MODE does that path first set recovery_state to BXE_RECOVERY_DONE, clear is_leader and release the leader lock. Otherwise, if state is CLOSED or ERROR it returns 0 with no further teardown. Otherwise it sets state to CLOSING_WAITING_HALT, disables TX, sets rx_mode to none, for a PF without grcdump_done drives the driver pulse and stops and saves statistics, drains the TX queues, then: for a VF does nothing here; for unload_mode other than UNLOAD_RECOVERY it calls bxe_chip_cleanup unless grcdump_done is set; for UNLOAD_RECOVERY it sends the unload request, disables the PF on non-E1x chips, disables and detaches interrupts and reports unload done. A PF then squeezes the queueable objects. For all device types it clears sp_state and port.pmf, frees the fastpath buffers and firmware stats memory, and sets state to BXE_STATE_CLOSED; bxe_free_mem is called only for a PF. A PF then checks parity attention (setting reset-in-progress and possibly reset-global) and may disable the close-the-gate; finally it reports the link and returns 0. The function contains no call that releases the core lock.
note: Both reviewer claims right: bxe_free_mem and bxe_squeeze_objects are PF-only (bxe.c:4331-4344) and the VF branch at 4296-4297 does no cleanup. Function really starts at 4208 (slice cut at 4101). Lock sentence: no unlock call appears in 4208-4377.

name: bxe_interrupt_alloc
prose: Precondition: sc is an initialized softc whose interrupt_mode selects the first mode to try (INTR_MODE_MSIX, INTR_MODE_MSI or INTR_MODE_INTX) and whose devinfo.pcie_cap_flags and num_queues are set. If interrupt_mode is positive it first reads the MSI-X and MSI vector counts from the bus when the capability flags are set. It then runs three sequential attempts, each skipped unless interrupt_mode equals its own mode: MSI-X (needs the capability and msix_count >= 2; requests min(num_queues + 1, msix_count) vectors; fewer than 2 granted is treated as failure; on success sets intr_count to the number granted and num_queues to that number minus one, and maps one IRQ resource per vector starting at rid 1), then MSI (needs the capability and msi_count >= 1; requests one vector, requires exactly one granted; sets intr_count and num_queues to 1 and maps rid 1), then INTx (sets intr_count and num_queues to 1 and maps rid 0 with RF_SHAREABLE). When an MSI-X or MSI attempt fails after vectors were allocated, it releases the already mapped IRQ resources (MSI-X) and calls pci_release_msi, resets intr_count and num_queues to 0 where they had been set, sets interrupt_mode to the next mode and falls through to it. If the INTx resource cannot be mapped it sets intr_count and num_queues to 0 and interrupt_mode to -1. Returns 1 if interrupt_mode is -1 at the end (and logs the failure) and 0 otherwise. If interrupt_mode on entry matches none of the three modes, no allocation is attempted and the function still returns 0 unless it was -1.
note: Slice started mid-body (8945); real function starts at bxe.c:8916 and is bxe_interrupt_alloc; read in full (8916-9107). The earlier prose claimed all failure paths fully clean up and was dropped only because of the unnamed head; the MSI-X partial map path releases earlier resources at 8991-9001, INTx failure at 9086-9090 releases nothing extra since nothing else is held.

name: elink_init_fpga
prose: Precondition: params and vars point to valid structures and params->sc is a softc for an FPGA configuration. It sets vars->duplex to DUPLEX_FULL and vars->flow_ctrl to ELINK_FLOW_CTRL_NONE; if the chip is not E1 it instead sets flow_ctrl to TX|RX and ORs the TX/RX flow-control-enabled bits into vars->link_status. On an E3 chip it copies params->req_line_speed[0] into vars->line_speed; ELINK_SPEED_AUTO_NEG is changed to 2500 and falls through to the 2500 case; 2500, 1000, 100 and 10 assign vars->link_status the corresponding full-duplex link constant (an assignment, so the flow-control bits set earlier are overwritten); any other speed returns ELINK_STATUS_ERROR immediately (leaving line_speed at the requested value and link_up unchanged). It then ORs in LINK_STATUS_LINK_UP and calls elink_umac_enable with the loopback argument 1 if loopback_mode is ELINK_LOOPBACK_UMAC, else 0. On a non-E3 chip it sets line_speed to ELINK_SPEED_10000, link_status to LINK_STATUS_LINK_UP|ELINK_LINK_10GTFD and calls elink_emac_enable with loopback 1 if loopback_mode is ELINK_LOOPBACK_EMAC, else 0. After either branch it sets vars->link_up to 1, calls elink_pbf_update when the chip is E1x, writes 0 to NIG_REG_EGRESS_DRAIN0_MODE + port*4, calls elink_update_mng with vars->link_status, and returns ELINK_STATUS_OK.
note: First reviewer claim (only UMAC/EMAC enabled) is true but the prose never claimed XMAC/BMAC: wrong as a criticism. Second reviewer claim (pbf_update, drain clear, update_mng not in function) is wrong: they are at bxe_elink.c:13667-13674. Real function is at 13617-13676 (slice 13384-13666). Added the E3 overwrite of link_status (13636-13646) as a true detail.

name: elink_ets_e3b0_sp_set_pri_cli_reg
prose: Precondition: params->sc and params->port are valid and sp_pri_to_cos points to at least max_num_of_cos bytes, where max_num_of_cos is ELINK_DCBX_E3B0_MAX_NUM_COS_PORT1 if params->port is nonzero, else ELINK_DCBX_E3B0_MAX_NUM_COS_PORT0. The function builds register values in locals first: the first loop takes each entry that is not DCBX_INVALID_COS as a strict-priority COS, and returns ELINK_STATUS_ERROR if the entry is >= ELINK_DCBX_MAX_NUM_COS or if its COS bit was already consumed (duplicate or out of the port's range); the second loop appends every COS index in increasing order that was not used as strict priority. If the number of priorities assigned does not equal max_num_of_cos it returns ELINK_STATUS_ERROR. Only after all checks pass does it write registers: for port 1 the low 32 bits to NIG_REG_P1_TX_ARB_PRIORITY_CLIENT2_LSB and the PBF value to PBF_REG_ETS_ARB_PRIORITY_CLIENT_P1; for port 0 the low 32 bits and bits 32-35 to the P0 NIG LSB and MSB registers and the PBF value to PBF_REG_ETS_ARB_PRIORITY_CLIENT_P0; then it returns ELINK_STATUS_OK. No register is written on any of the three error returns.
note: Reviewer 1 (partial sp_pri_to_cos is rejected) is wrong: partial arrays are accepted and the remaining COSes are appended (bxe_elink.c:1816-1830). Reviewer 2 is right: the pri_set != max_num_of_cos error return (1832-1836) was missing. Function really at 1770-1857 (slice 1589-1842).

name: ciss_periodic
prose: Precondition: arg is the ciss_softc pointer that the periodic callout was armed with, and sc->ciss_cfg is mapped. If sc->ciss_cfg->heartbeat equals the saved sc->ciss_heartbeat it increments ciss_heart_attack; when that counter reaches exactly 3 it logs ADAPTER HEARTBEAT FAILED, calls ciss_disable_adapter and returns without sending a NOP, restarting notify or rescheduling the callout. If the heartbeat differs it saves the new value and resets ciss_heart_attack to 0. In every case that did not return early (heartbeat changed, or unchanged for the first or second time), if the global ciss_nop_message_heartbeat is nonzero and ciss_get_request succeeds it fills in a NOP message command with completion routine ciss_nop_complete and calls ciss_start; a nonzero ciss_start result is only logged and the request is not released here, and a ciss_get_request failure is silently ignored. Then if CISS_FLAG_NOTIFY_OK is not set in sc->ciss_flags it calls ciss_notify_event, and it finally calls callout_reset to run itself again after CISS_HEARTBEAT_RATE * hz ticks.
note: Reviewer 2 (round 15) right: NOP, notify and reschedule happen also when the heartbeat is unchanged but the counter is below 3 (ciss.c:3506-3551). Reviewer 1 (original, heart_attack direction reversed) was about an older prose; current code increments on unchanged (3507). Real function at 3491-3552 (slice 3323-3585). Whether ciss_start frees the request on failure was not read.

name: aw_clk_np_register
prose: Precondition: clkdom and clkdef are valid pointers to a clock domain and an aw_clk_np_def. It calls clknode_create with aw_np_clknode_class and the generic clknode definition inside clkdef; if that returns NULL it returns 1 and nothing is copied or registered. Otherwise it copies offset, the n field (shift, width, value, flags) and the p field (shift, width, value, flags), gate_shift, lock_shift, lock_retries and flags from clkdef into the node's softc, computes n.mask and p.mask as ((1 << width) - 1) << shift (int arithmetic, so a width of 31 or more is not safe), calls clknode_register(clkdom, clk), and returns 0.
note: Slice 253-269 started mid-body; function is aw_clk_np_register at aw_clk_np.c:233-269 (head cut by slice). Old prose omitted the n field; added from lines 245-251. Whether clknode_register can fail or takes ownership was not read; return value of clknode_register is ignored at 266.

name: t3_aq100x_phy_prep
prose: Precondition: pinfo points to an initialised port_info whose adapter is valid, phy_addr selects the PHY and mdio_ops gives the MDIO accessors. It initialises pinfo->phy with cphy_init (aq100x_ops, supported-feature mask, "1000/10GBASE-T"), toggles a GPIO bit (F_GPIO10_OUT_VAL if phy_addr is nonzero, else F_GPIO6_OUT_VAL) low then high to hard-reset the PHY with msleep delays, waits 1000 ms, then polls the PMA/PMD MII_BMCR register until BMCR_RESET clears (up to 500 polls of 10 ms). If that BMCR read returns an error or the value 0xffff it logs a warning and jumps to done; if BMCR_RESET is still set after the polling it logs a timeout warning and jumps to done. Otherwise it reads the firmware version, the BMCR power-down bit and the XAUI/1000-X settings, emitting CH_WARN warnings only when they look wrong, calls aq100x_set_defaults and discards its result. The value returned (at done) is the variable err, which is only ever assigned by the mdio_read inside the polling loop; so it returns that read's error code if one occurred, and 0 in all other cases, including the 0xffff-read and the reset-timeout exits (which are meant to let adapter preparation succeed). No locks are taken.
note: Slice 508-541 started at the timeout exit; the function is t3_aq100x_phy_prep at cxgb_aq100x.c:462-541 (read in full). Earlier prose said the result is the error from 'earlier steps'; only the loop read sets err (490). The later mdio_reads are cast to void (512,518,527-528,533).

name: t4_write_flash
prose: Precondition: data points to at least n readable bytes. Returns -EINVAL immediately, before touching the hardware, if addr is >= adapter->params.sf_size or if (addr & 0xff) + n exceeds SF_PAGE_SIZE. Otherwise it sends a write-enable and then the page-program command with the byte-swapped address through sf1_write, then feeds the data to sf1_write in chunks of up to 4 bytes (each chunk assembled most significant byte first into a word, and passed through cpu_to_be32 only when byte_oriented is zero), then calls flash_wait_op with 8 attempts. If any of those sf1_write or flash_wait_op calls returns nonzero, it writes 0 to A_SF_OP (releasing the serial flash) and returns that code; the page may then be partly programmed. On success of the programming steps it writes 0 to A_SF_OP, reads the whole page back with t4_read_flash (same byte_oriented value) and returns that call's error code if it fails; then compares the n bytes at addr's offset in the page with the supplied data, logging an error and returning -EIO on mismatch, else returning 0. The serial flash is unlocked (A_SF_OP written 0) on every return after the -EINVAL check, but not on the -EINVAL return, where it was never locked.
note: Reviewer 2 (round 15) right in wording only: the early -EINVAL return at t4_hw.c:3953-3954 does not write A_SF_OP; prose now says so. Reviewer 1 (original, byte_oriented semantics reversed) concerned an older prose; the new prose describes the code literally (3962-3970) and does not state the resulting flash byte order. Specific errno values from sf1_write, flash_wait_op and t4_read_flash not read. Real function at 3946-3997 (slice 3688-3952).

name: ktls_act_open_cpl_size
prose: Precondition: none; isipv6 may be true or false. Returns sizeof(struct cpl_t6_act_open_req6) if isipv6 is true, otherwise sizeof(struct cpl_t6_act_open_req); no other value is returned and it has no side effects.
note: Read in full at t6_kern_tls.c:138-146. Function only chooses between two sizeof values; contract left empty because the result is a struct size not a plain integer relation.

name: cudbg_collect
prose: Precondition: handle points to a struct cudbg_private whose dbg_init (dbg_bitmap, adap, verbose, print, use_flash) is set up, outbuf is writable for *outbuf_size bytes and outbuf_size is writable. It writes the global cudbg_hdr at the start of outbuf, and treats the call as extended mode (flag_ext) if cudbg_hdr->data_len is nonzero when read after those writes. If use_flash is set and t4_get_flash_params fails, use_flash is cleared. If *outbuf_size is smaller than sizeof(struct cudbg_entity_hdr) * CUDBG_MAX_ENTITY it returns CUDBG_STATUS_SMALL_BUFF without updating *outbuf_size. Otherwise it loops over the entity numbers 1 to CUDBG_MAX_ENTITY-1 selected by the bitmap (or all, if the CUDBG_ALL bit is set), skipping the EXT entity: it obtains an entity header (in ext mode via get_next_ext_entity_hdr, whose nonzero return makes the function return that code immediately; in normal mode via get_entity_hdr, whose nonzero result is only stored in cudbg_hdr->hdr_flags), skips large entities when the remaining buffer is at most BUFFER_WARN_LIMIT (recording them for a retry) and firmware-dependent entities when firmware is not attached, and otherwise runs the entity's process function. If an entity fails, its header size is set to 0 and the offset is restored to its start; its hdr_flags, sys_err and sys_warn are recorded in its header, sys_err turning the status into CUDBG_SYSTEM_ERROR, and none of this is returned to the caller. A second loop retries the entities that were skipped as large, with the same header handling and the same early return on a get_next_ext_entity_hdr failure. In normal mode total_size grows by each entity size; it then sets cudbg_hdr->data_len and *outbuf_size to total_size, adds ext_size to *outbuf_size in ext mode, and returns 0, so per-entity failures do not change the return value. Entities are optionally written to flash through wr_entity_to_flash when use_flash is set.
note: Reviewer (round 15) partly right/partly wrong: he says *outbuf_size excludes ext_size, but cudbg_lib.c:516-517 adds ext_size when flag_ext; he says rc stays nonzero, but the function returns the literal 0 at 519 (rc is returned only at err: 521 on SMALL_BUFF or a get_next_ext_entity_hdr failure). Function really starts at 202 (slice 261-512 cut head). Read in full 202-522; the process_entity callbacks and helper functions were not read.

name: process_socket_event
prose: Precondition: ep points to a valid c4iw_ep with com.so set. It reads ep->com.state once into a local. If the state is DEAD it only logs a trace message and returns. If the state is CONNECTING it calls process_connected and returns. If the state is LISTEN it takes the listen socket lock, then loops: solisten_dequeue(listen_so, &new_so, SOCK_NONBLOCK); if that returns an error it returns at once without calling SOLISTEN_UNLOCK itself (the code comment says solisten_dequeue returns with the lock released); otherwise it calls process_newconn(lep, new_so), re-takes the listen lock and repeats while listen_so->sol_qlen is nonzero, and finally unlocks and returns. For other states: if so->so_error is set it calls process_conn_error and returns; else if the receive side has SBS_CANTRCVMORE set and the saved state is <= CLOSING it calls process_peer_close and returns unless SS_ISDISCONNECTED is also set, in which case it continues; then if SS_ISDISCONNECTED is set it calls process_close_complete and returns; else if the receive buffer has data (sbused) it calls process_data and returns. If none of those apply, then in a kernel built with INVARIANTS the MPASS asserts the state is MPA_REQ_RCVD or MORIBUND (and panics otherwise); when assertions are compiled out and the state is neither MPA_REQ_RCVD nor MORIBUND, an Unprocessed socket event error is logged; no handler is called. The function returns nothing.
note: Round 15 reviewer is partly right: MPASS at cm.c:1194 asserts the state, so with INVARIANTS no log happens for other states; the log at 1196-1200 only matters when MPASS is compiled out. Earlier reviewer comments (multiple handlers, lock on dequeue error) are covered by 1133-1158 and 1167-1181. Function at 1112-1202 (slice 1027-1278). Whether solisten_dequeue really unlocks on error was not checked in the socket code.

name: send_mpa_reply
prose: Precondition: ep points to a valid endpoint with mpa_attr, ird, ord and com.so set, and pdata points to at least plen bytes when plen is nonzero. It sizes the MPA message as sizeof(struct mpa_message) + plen, plus sizeof(struct mpa_v2_conn_params) when mpa_attr.version is 2 and enhanced_rdma_conn is set. It returns -ENOMEM if the M_NOWAIT malloc of that buffer fails, with ep unchanged. It then fills the key (MPA_KEY_REP), flags (MPA_CRC if crc_enabled, MPA_MARKERS if the global markers_enabled), revision and private_data_size; in the v2 enhanced case it also sets MPA_ENHANCED_RDMA_CONN, adds the v2 parameter size, fills ird and ord from ep->ird and ep->ord, adds the peer-to-peer model bit and an RDMA-write or read RTR bit only when the global peer2peer is set, ep->mpa_attr.p2p_type is not disabled and the global p2p_type is the matching value, copies the v2 parameters into private_data, and copies plen bytes of pdata after them only if ep->plen is nonzero (the condition tests ep->plen, the copy length is the argument plen). In the other case it copies plen bytes of pdata when plen is nonzero. It then allocates an mbuf chain with m_getm (M_NOWAIT); if that fails it frees the MPA buffer and returns -ENOMEM before changing ep. Otherwise it copies the message into the mbufs, frees the MPA buffer, sets ep->com.state to MPA_REP_SENT, adds the message length to ep->snd_seq, calls sosend with MSG_DONTWAIT passing the mbuf, and returns the negated sosend return value (0 on success). State and snd_seq are updated before sosend is called and are not rolled back if it fails.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: pdata copy length is plen, while the condition tests ep->plen (cm.c:1587-1589); prose rewritten. Function at 1521-1609 (slice 1531-1784 cut head). Read in full. Whether sosend frees the mbuf on failure was not checked.

name: poll_cq
prose: Precondition: cq is a valid t4_cq and wq is either NULL or the t4_wq of the QP that owns the next CQE; cqe, cqe_flushed, cookie and credit point to writable storage. It sets *cqe_flushed and *credit to 0, then calls t4_next_cqe(cq, &hw_cqe); if that returns nonzero it returns that value and consumes nothing. Once a CQE has been fetched, every later path ends at skip_cqe, which consumes it (t4_swcq_consume for a software CQE, otherwise t4_hwcq_consume) and returns ret. Paths with ret = -EAGAIN and no completion copied: wq is NULL; wq->flushed and the CQE is not a software CQE; FW_RI_TERMINATE opcode; a read-response CQE of type 1, an unsolicited one (WRID_STAG 1) or one for an unsignaled read (each of the first two also marks the wq in error when CQE_STATUS is nonzero); an RQ completion when the receive queue is empty (also marks the wq in error); and a send completion whose SQ index differs from wq->sq.cidx, which is stored in the software SQ entry and followed by flush_completed_wrs. For a C4IW_DRAIN_OPCODE CQE it sets *cookie to the drain cookie, copies the CQE to *cqe and returns 0 without consuming any SQ or RQ entry. Otherwise, if the CQE status is nonzero or the wq is in error it sets *cqe_flushed to 1 only when the status is T4_ERR_SWFLUSH (else 0) and marks the wq in error; an RQ completion whose MSN differs from wq->rq.msn is marked with T4_ERR_MSN and the wq is put in error. On the proc_cqe path it copies the CQE to *cqe, and for an SQ completion adjusts sq.in_use, sets sq.cidx, sets *cookie to the stored wr_id, consumes the SQ entry and calls flush_completed_wrs; for an RQ completion it sets *cookie to the RQ wr_id and consumes the RQ entry. Those proc_cqe paths return 0.
note: Round 15 reviewer is wrong: poll_cq calls t4_next_cqe at cq.c:499 (not t4_next_hw_cqe); first reviewer (drain opcode) is right and the prose now says drain consumes no SQ/RQ entry (539-543). Function at 491-704 (slice 512-788 cut head). Read in full. Helper functions (t4_next_cqe, flush_completed_wrs, create_read_req_cqe) not read.

name: c4iw_modify_qp
prose: Precondition: rhp, qhp and attrs are valid and the caller does not hold qhp->mutex. The function takes qhp->mutex and, after releasing it at the out label, runs deferred actions outside the lock. If mask has C4IW_QP_ATTR_VALID_MODIFY: it returns -EIO if the QP is not in C4IW_QP_STATE_IDLE; otherwise it applies the RDMA read/write/bind flags, and returns -EINVAL if max_ord exceeds c4iw_max_read_depth or max_ird exceeds cur_max_read_depth(rhp) (attributes are stored into qhp->attr only after all checks pass). If C4IW_QP_ATTR_NEXT_STATE is not in mask, or the current state already equals next_state, it returns the current ret (0 after a successful attribute update) with no state change. It returns -EINPROGRESS if the current state is ERROR or later and the requested state is TERMINATE. Then by current state: IDLE accepts RTS (needs both C4IW_QP_ATTR_LLP_STREAM_HANDLE and C4IW_QP_ATTR_MPA_ATTR else -EINVAL; sets the mpa attributes, endpoint and RTS state, takes an endpoint reference with c4iw_get_ep, calls rdma_init and goes to the err path if it fails) and ERROR (sets ERROR and flush_qp), other targets give -EINVAL. RTS accepts CLOSING (rdma_fini, err path on failure; for a non-internal call it also takes an extra endpoint reference and schedules a disconnect), TERMINATE (sets state and error codes; non-internal calls schedule terminate and disconnect, internal calls call rdma_fini and go to the err path on failure, otherwise return normally), and ERROR (always takes the err path, which for a non-internal call also schedules an abort-disconnect), other targets give -EINVAL. CLOSING returns -EINVAL for a non-internal call unless it is a kernel QP (no uobject) going to ERROR; it accepts IDLE (flush_qp, state IDLE, drops the endpoint with c4iw_put_ep) and ERROR (err path), other targets give -EINVAL via the err path. ERROR accepts only IDLE, and only if the SQ and RQ are empty (else -EINVAL). TERMINATE: a non-internal call gets -EINVAL, an internal call takes the err path; any unknown state gives -EINVAL via the err path. The err path clears llp_stream_handle and qhp->ep, forces state ERROR, flushes the QP, wakes waiters, and sets flags so that the endpoint is aborted and dereferenced (one c4iw_put_ep for the QP's reference, and for a scheduled disconnect another one after __c4iw_ep_disconnect). The return value is ret: 0 on success and on the no-op cases, or the negative error above; the err path leaves ret as it was, so it can return 0 while moving the QP to ERROR.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: internal RTS->TERMINATE with rdma_fini success does 'break' then 'goto out' (qp.c:1569-1575, 1643), not the err path; prose rewritten. Earlier reviewer is also right (no-op returns 0; err paths change state before failing). Real function at 1436-1684 (slice 1345-1645). Read in full; the callees rdma_init, rdma_fini, flush_qp, post_terminate, __c4iw_ep_disconnect not read.

name: update_hw_clip_table
prose: Precondition: the caller holds clip_db_lock (asserted with mtx_assert). It calls begin_synchronized_op(sc, NULL, HOLD_LOCK, "t4clip") and returns its error if nonzero, in which case no synchronized operation is open. Otherwise, if hw_all_ok(sc) is false it ends the synchronized operation and returns 0 with sc->clip_pending untouched. Otherwise it processes sc->clip_pending from the head until the queue is empty or it stops. For an entry with clip_idx == -1 (pending add): if both ce->refcount and cde->krn_ref are 0 it removes and frees the entry (and frees the database entry when its adp_ref reaches 0); otherwise it calls add_lip: FW_ENOMEM makes it stop and return 0 leaving that entry (and the later ones) queued, any other nonzero error is logged, stops the loop and is returned with the entry still queued, and on success the entry is dequeued and marked not pending. For an entry with a valid clip_idx (pending delete): if both counts are 0 it calls del_lip, logs a nonzero result, treats FW_EPROTO as success, returns any other error leaving the entry queued, and otherwise removes and frees the entry as above; if either count is nonzero it just dequeues the entry and clears pending. On every return after a successful begin_synchronized_op it calls end_synchronized_op(sc, LOCK_HELD); clip_db_lock is still held on return. It returns 0 if the queue was drained or it stopped on FW_ENOMEM or on hw_all_ok being false, and otherwise the error from add_lip or del_lip.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: on FW_ENOMEM earlier entries may already have been removed (t4_clip.c:581-608), so the queue is only left unprocessed from the failing entry on. Original reviewer is right too: 0 is returned without draining on FW_ENOMEM or !hw_all_ok. Function at 567-658 (slice 509-774). Read in full. add_lip/del_lip internals not read; note del_lip logs ip before it is filled (line 634-635) which is not described.

name: toe_capability
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the adapter's synchronized-operation lock (ASSERT_SYNCHRONIZED_OP) and vi is a VI of the adapter. It returns ENODEV if the adapter is not offload capable and ENXIO if hw_all_ok fails. When enable is true: in a KERN_TLS build, if KERN_TLS_ON is set on a T6 adapter it counts the interfaces with IFCAP_TXTLS enabled and returns EAGAIN if any, otherwise calls t6_config_kern_tls(sc, false) and returns its error if nonzero; this happens before the check for TOE already being enabled, so it also runs when TOE is already on. Then if IFCAP_TOE is already set on vi->ifp it returns 0 with no counter change. Otherwise it runs vi_init on vi and on the port's first VI if their VI_INIT_DONE flags are not set (returning a failure code), and if offload_map already has the port's bit set it increments pi->uld_vis and returns 0. Otherwise it activates the TOM ULD if it is not active (logging when the error is EAGAIN and returning any nonzero error), tries to activate the iWARP and iSCSI ULDs ignoring their results, then increments pi->uld_vis and sets the port's bit in offload_map if the count was previously 0, and returns 0. When enable is false: if IFCAP_TOE is not set it returns 0; otherwise it decrements pi->uld_vis and clears the port's offload_map bit when the count reaches 0, then returns 0. The MPASS checks assert expected states only in builds with assertions.
note: Both reviewers right: the already-enabled case is not a pure no-op because the KERN_TLS check and t6_config_kern_tls precede it (t4_main.c:13338-13375), and the offload_map bit can already be set when another VI of the port had TOE (13388-13393). Function at 13324-13430 (slice 13260-13515). Read in full; callee internals not read.

name: service_iq_fl
prose: Precondition: iq is a valid ingress queue in IQS_BUSY state with IQ_HAS_FL set. Only when INET or INET6 is compiled in, if IQ_ADJ_CREDIT is set it clears the flag and checks the descriptor at cidx: if its generation bit does not equal iq->gen it flushes all LRO state, writes the SGE GTS register crediting one descriptor, and returns 0 without refilling the freelist; if it matches, the count of consumed descriptors starts at 1. It then processes descriptors while their generation bit equals iq->gen, with limit = budget if budget is nonzero, else iq->qsize / 16. For a free-list-buffer response it may advance to the next rx buffer, and when the hardware consumer index has moved by more than 4 since the snapshot it refills the freelist (64 buffers) under the FL lock; a CPL_RX_PKT is passed to eth_rx and any other one gets its payload from get_fl_payload and then goes to the CPL handler table; if eth_rx returns nonzero or get_fl_payload returns NULL the loop is left without consuming the current descriptor. A CPL-type response calls the CPL handler for its opcode. An interrupt-type response panics if its qid is below 1024, otherwise calls t4_an_handler. An unknown response type triggers KASSERT and logs an error (continuing if assertions are off). Each processed descriptor advances cidx, wrapping and flipping the generation bit at sidx. When the consumed count reaches limit, it writes the GTS register with that count and, if LRO is enabled, not sorted-before-LRO and sc->lro_timeout is nonzero, flushes inactive LRO entries; with a nonzero budget it then returns EINPROGRESS directly (no freelist refill at that point); with budget 0 it resets the count to 0 and continues. At the common exit (generation mismatch or the early exits) when IQ_LRO_ENABLED is set it holds back one credit and sets IQ_ADJ_CREDIT if the count is positive and more than 8 LRO mbufs are pending, otherwise flushes all LRO state; it writes the GTS register with the remaining count, refills the freelist with 64 buffers under the FL lock, adds the freelist to the starved list if refill_fl reports starvation, and returns 0.
note: Reviewers right: early IQ_ADJ_CREDIT mismatch skips the refill (t4_sge.c:1625-1634); with budget 0 the limit path writes GTS, resets ndescs and continues, and also optionally flushes inactive LRO (1714-1729). Function at 1603-1755 (slice 1586-1842). Read in full; callees not read.

name: do_peer_close
prose: Precondition: called as the CPL_PEER_CLOSE handler with m == NULL (KASSERTed) and a tid that lookup_tid maps to a toepcb with a valid inp. It returns 0 on every path. If toep->flags has TPF_SYNQE it returns immediately without taking any lock. Otherwise it enters the vnet and network epoch and write-locks the inp. If TPF_ABORT_SHUTDOWN is set it skips to the common exit. Otherwise, when the ULP mode is TCPDDP it takes DDP_LOCK and calls handle_ddp_close only if a DDP buffer is active, then releases DDP_LOCK; it calls socantrcvmore on the socket and sets tp->rcv_nxt from the CPL (the old and new values are compared only in a KASSERT, and not for RDMA or T6+ iSCSI modes). Then by TCP state: SYN_RECEIVED sets t_starttime and, like ESTABLISHED, moves to CLOSE_WAIT; FIN_WAIT_1 moves to CLOSING; FIN_WAIT_2 restores the socket protocol, detaches the toepcb from the tcpcb, calls tcp_twstart, exits the epoch and vnet, takes the inp write lock again, calls final_cpl_received(toep) and returns 0 without passing through the common exit; any other state only logs an error. All paths other than the FIN_WAIT_2 one reach the common exit, which drops the inp write lock, exits the epoch and restores the vnet before returning 0.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the FIN_WAIT_2 path does exit the epoch and re-acquire the inp lock (t4_cpl_io.c:1493-1503); the old text was misleading and is rewritten. Original reviewer is right that the SYNQE/ABORT_SHUTDOWN early paths and default state skip the rcv_nxt/state change (1427-1437, 1451, 1505-1507); note ABORT_SHUTDOWN skips before rcv_nxt update. Function at 1408-1514 (slice 1281-1534). Read in full; final_cpl_received (which presumably releases the inp lock) was not read.

name: insert_ddp_data
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the inp write lock and the DDP lock of toep (both asserted), and n bytes of data were placed by DDP before the connection fell out of DDP. It adds n to tp->rcv_nxt and, unless USE_DDP_RX_FLOW_CONTROL is defined, KASSERTs tp->rcv_wnd >= n and subtracts n from tp->rcv_wnd. Then while toep->ddp.active_count > 0 it takes the active buffer. In DDP_RCVBUF mode it places min(n, remaining space of the buffer), queues that many bytes with queue_ddp_rcvbuf_mbuf if nonzero, calls complete_ddp_buffer and reduces n by the amount placed. Otherwise it takes the buffer's AIO job, places min(n, bytes still wanted by the job), counts statistics, and: if the cancel function can no longer be cleared (a cancel is in progress) it only adds the placed amount to job->aio_received; else if some data was received in total (copied + placed != 0) it completes the job with that byte count; else it tries to put the job back at the head of the pending queue (incrementing waiting_count) and cancels it if that is not possible; then it reduces n by the amount placed and calls complete_ddp_buffer. After the loop MPASS(n == 0) asserts (in INVARIANTS builds only) that all n bytes were placed; in other builds a nonzero n would be left unplaced and the function returns nothing.
note: Round 15 reviewer is wrong: there is an MPASS(n == 0) after the loop (t4_ddp.c:537). Earlier reviewer's points (rcv_wnd conditional, n may be left unplaced without INVARIANTS) are covered. Function at 461-538 (slice 258-536). Read in full; complete_ddp_buffer and queue_ddp_rcvbuf_mbuf not read.

name: t4_pmtu_update
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the inp write lock (asserted), mtu is positive (MPASS) and seq is in network byte order, snd_una and snd_max being in host order. It converts seq to host order. It returns without changing anything if the ULP mode is ULP_MODE_NONE and seq is outside [tp->snd_una, tp->snd_max) (the range check is skipped for other ULP modes), or if the MTU index chosen as the largest table entry not above mtu is not smaller than toep->params.mtu_idx (the path MTU is never raised), or if start_wrq_wr for the control queue fails (in which case it logs an error). Otherwise it builds and commits an atomic compound work request with two SET_TCB_FIELD operations (one setting the T_MAXSEG field to the new index, one clearing the timestamp field to trigger a retransmit), then sets toep->params.mtu_idx to the new index, sets tp->t_maxseg to the table MTU minus the IPv6 or IPv4 header and TCP header sizes, and sets toep->params.emss to that value minus TCPOLEN_TSTAMP_APPA when TF_RCVD_TSTMP is set. It then calls send_mss_flowc_wr, which logs an error and sends nothing if tx credits or tx sdesc entries are insufficient or the work request cannot be allocated, and otherwise sends a flowc work request carrying the new emss. Finally, if sc->tt.update_hc_on_pmtu_change is nonzero it calls tcp_hc_updatemtu with the foreign address and fib number and the requested mtu. It returns nothing.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: send_mss_flowc_wr logs CH_ERR when credits/txsd are exhausted or allocation fails (t4_tom.c:873-883), so the drop is not silent. Original reviewer (range check only for ULP_MODE_NONE, WR may fail, seq network order) matches 925-931, 944-949, 919. Function at 903-989 (slice 763-1019). Read in full along with send_mss_flowc_wr 864-901.

name: cyapa_attach
prose: Precondition: dev is a newbus device whose softc is a cyapa_softc not yet attached. It sets sc->reporting_mode to 1 first, then calls init_device(dev, &cap, 0); if that returns nonzero it returns ENXIO (reporting_mode has already been set, but no mutex, knlist, evdev, hook or device node exists yet). Otherwise it initialises the softc mutex and the selinfo knlist on it, stores dev, computes the X/Y resolution and physical size and the button mask from the capability data, prints a summary line, fills in the hw and mode structures (PS/2 protocol, packet size, rate 100, resolution 4) and sets the interrupt hook function to cyapa_start with dev as argument. With EVDEV_SUPPORT it allocates an evdev, sets its name, phys, id, flags and supported events/keys/axes, and registers it; if evdev_register fails it destroys the mutex and returns ENOMEM (the evdev is not freed on that path and the knlist is not destroyed). It then calls config_intrhook_establish; if that fails it frees the evdev (with EVDEV_SUPPORT), destroys the mutex and returns ENOMEM (the knlist is not destroyed). On success it creates the /dev/cyapa<unit> node with owner root, group wheel, mode 0600, sets si_drv1 to the softc, and returns 0.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: reporting_mode IS set, at cyapa.c:523, but before init_device, not after (the prose wrongly put it after success); it is also set when init_device fails. Added the paths that do not free the evdev (601-604). Real function at 514-622 (slice 528-793 cut the head). Read in full.

name: dc_rxeof
prose: Precondition: sc is a valid dc_softc and the caller holds the softc lock (DC_LOCK_ASSERT). Starting at sc->dc_cdata.dc_rx_prod it loops over RX descriptors while IFF_DRV_RUNNING is set on the interface. The loop is left, and the current index stored into sc->dc_cdata.dc_rx_prod, when (with DEVICE_POLLING and IFCAP_POLLING enabled) sc->rxcycles is not positive, when a descriptor still has DC_RXSTAT_OWN set, or when IFF_DRV_RUNNING has been cleared; sc->rxcycles is decremented once per descriptor examined in polling mode. Each descriptor examined past the ownership check increments rx_npkts, including PNIC-workaround fragments, errored frames, and frames that are dropped. On PNIC-bug hardware (DC_PNIC_RX_BUG_WAR) a non-whole-frame descriptor is skipped until its last fragment, then dc_pnic_rx_bug_war repairs it. For a descriptor with DC_RXSTAT_RXERR that is not a giant frame without another error flag, it increments IFCOUNTER_IERRORS (and IFCOUNTER_COLLISIONS if DC_RXSTAT_COLLSEEN) and calls dc_discard_rxbuf; if DC_RXSTAT_CRCERR is set it continues with the next descriptor, otherwise it clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING, calls dc_init_locked(sc) and returns rx_npkts immediately without storing dc_rx_prod. For a good frame it subtracts ETHER_CRC_LEN and either (on __NO_STRICT_ALIGNMENT) replaces the ring buffer with dc_newbuf, or on dc_newbuf failure discards the buffer and increments IFCOUNTER_IQDROPS, or (strict alignment) copies it with m_devget and discards the original buffer, counting IFCOUNTER_IQDROPS if m_devget returns NULL. A delivered frame increments IFCOUNTER_IPACKETS and is passed to if_input with the softc lock dropped around the call and re-taken afterwards. The function returns rx_npkts; the softc lock is held on return.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the early return after dc_init_locked at if_dc.c:2914-2916 does not update dc_rx_prod (stored only at 2961). Old prose also said 'a lone CRC error' for the reinit case; code reinitialises for any non-CRC error. Real function at 2847-2963 (slice 2856-3125 cut head). Read in full; dc_pnic_rx_bug_war, dc_discard_rxbuf, dc_newbuf not read.

name: pnphy_service
prose: Precondition: sc, mii and mii->mii_media.ifm_cur are valid. For MII_MEDIACHG with the interface not IFF_UP it falls out of the switch; with the interface up, a current subtype of IFM_100_TX or IFM_10_T sets mii_media_active to IFM_ETHER plus that subtype (adding IFM_FDX if the entry has it), calls MIIBUS_STATCHG and returns 0 without calling PHY_STATUS or mii_phy_update; any other subtype returns EINVAL with no media state changed. For MII_TICK with the interface not IFF_UP it returns 0 immediately without calling PHY_STATUS or mii_phy_update; with the interface up, and for MII_POLLSTAT, MII_MEDIACHG while down, or any other cmd value, it calls PHY_STATUS(sc) and mii_phy_update(sc, cmd) and returns 0.
note: Both reviewers right: MII_MEDIACHG supported subtypes return after MIIBUS_STATCHG (pnphy.c:159-171), and MII_TICK with the interface down returns 0 early (181-182); the old prose got MII_TICK wrong. Real function at 140-193 (slice 1-225). Read in full.

name: qman_portals_fdt_attach
prose: Precondition: dev is a newbus device with an OFW node. It reads the address/size cell counts of the parent node and of its own node with get_addr_props, then loads the "ranges" property. If the property has fewer than addr + paddr + size cells it returns ENXIO at once without calling OF_prop_free on the ranges buffer and without setting sc->sc_dp_pa or sc_dp_size. Otherwise it decodes the property into portal physical address (the child base plus parent base) and size, frees the buffer with OF_prop_free, and stores sc_dp_pa and sc_dp_size. It then iterates the child nodes, stopping once mp_ncpus portals have been counted; children not compatible with "fsl,qman-portal" are skipped, as are children for which no CPU handle can be found (neither the cpu-handle property nor qman_portal_find_cpu gives a positive value). If the CPU node's "reg" cannot be read it prints a message and returns ENXIO immediately, without calling qman_portals_detach. After counting the CPU, a child whose devinfo setup, "reg" or "interrupts" processing fails is skipped (after freeing the resource list and destroying the devinfo where they had been created). If dpaa_portal_alloc_res fails it frees the resource list, destroys the devinfo, calls qman_portals_detach(dev) and returns ENXIO. After the loop it destroys the devinfo and returns the result of qman_portals_attach(dev).
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: no devinfo exists for the current child when the CPU reg read fails (qman_fdt.c:223-226), so the old claim of an undestroyed current devinfo was wrong. Round 2 reviewer right: no OF_prop_free on the short-ranges return (186-187). Original reviewer right: reg/interrupt/devinfo failures continue (230-248). Real function at 158-263 (slice 1-254). Read in full. A devinfo set up in an earlier loop iteration is not destroyed per iteration (only the last one at 255); not described further.

name: drm_context_switch
prose: Precondition: dev is a valid DRM device. It atomically tests and sets bit 0 of dev->context_flag; if the bit was already set it logs "Reentering" and returns -EBUSY, leaving the bit set. Otherwise it logs the switch and, if new equals dev->last_context, clears bit 0 again; in every case that reaches this point it returns 0 (when new differs from dev->last_context the flag is left set). It does not itself change dev->last_context.
note: Round 15 reviewer right: the precondition 'flag clear' was wrong because the already-set case returns -EBUSY (drm_context.c:264-267). Original reviewer right: flag is cleared when new == last_context (271-274). Function at 262-277 (slice 252-492), read in full.

name: drm_switchctx
prose: Precondition: dev, data (a struct drm_ctx) and file_priv are valid. It logs ctx->handle and returns drm_context_switch(dev, dev->last_context, ctx->handle) unchanged: -EBUSY if dev->context_flag bit 0 was already set (flag left as it was), otherwise 0, with the bit cleared again when ctx->handle equals dev->last_context and left set otherwise.
note: Round 15 reviewer right: no precondition on the flag is needed; the already-set case is handled by drm_context_switch returning -EBUSY (drm_context.c:264-267, 421-428). Original reviewer's point (0 returned with no switch when handle equals last_context) matches 271-274. Function at 421-428 read in full.

name: drm_setmaster_ioctl
prose: Precondition: dev and file_priv are valid and file_priv->minor is non-NULL (it is dereferenced); data is unused. It returns 0 immediately if file_priv->is_master is already set. It returns -EINVAL if file_priv->minor->master is set and differs from file_priv->master, if file_priv->master is NULL, or if file_priv->minor->master is set at all. Otherwise, holding DRM_LOCK(dev), it stores drm_master_get(file_priv->master) into file_priv->minor->master and sets file_priv->is_master to 1; if dev->driver->master_set exists and returns nonzero it sets is_master back to 0 and drops the master reference with drm_master_put on minor->master. The result of master_set is not returned: after the lock is released the function returns 0 in every case that passes the checks.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: minor is dereferenced at drm_stub.c:181 so it cannot be NULL; precondition fixed. Original reviewer right: master_set failure is swallowed and 0 is returned (193-202). Function at 173-203 (slice 1-252). Read in full; drm_master_put's effect on the minor->master pointer not read.

name: drm_crtc_helper_set_config
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the mode config lock as the DRM code expects (not checked here). Returns -EINVAL if set is NULL, set->crtc is NULL, or set->crtc->helper_private is NULL. If set->mode is NULL it sets set->fb to NULL; if set->fb is then NULL it returns drm_crtc_helper_disable(set->crtc) directly, before allocating any backup, so the crtc is disabled and nothing else in this function runs. Otherwise it allocates zeroed backup arrays for all crtcs, encoders and connectors (M_NOWAIT), returning -ENOMEM and freeing what was allocated if any allocation fails, with nothing modified; it copies the current crtc/encoder/connector structs into them and works out whether the change is a full mode set (mode_changed: no current fb, different depth or bits per pixel, a different mode, a changed encoder or crtc binding, or a flip needed without a mode_set_base hook) or only a flip (fb_changed: same-format fb or changed x/y). It rebinds connectors to encoders using best_encoder for the connectors named in set; a NULL best_encoder, or an encoder that cannot work with the new crtc (drm_encoder_crtc_ok), leads to failure with -EINVAL. If mode_changed, it sets crtc->enabled from drm_helper_crtc_in_use; only if the crtc is in use does it call drm_crtc_helper_set_mode (failure restores the old fb and gives -EINVAL) and turns the listed connectors' DPMS on; in both cases it then calls drm_helper_disable_unused_functions. Else if fb_changed it updates x, y and fb and calls crtc_funcs->mode_set_base; a nonzero return restores the old fb and fails with that code. If neither flag is set nothing is applied. On success it frees the three backups and returns 0. On any failure it copies the saved crtc/encoder/connector structs back, tries to restore the old mode with drm_crtc_helper_set_mode when mode_changed was set (only logging an error if that fails), frees the backups and returns the error.
note: Both reviewers right: the set->fb == NULL path (including set->mode == NULL) returns drm_crtc_helper_disable at drm_crtc_helper.c:578-588 with no backup and no mode applied, which the old prose described as decoupling encoders with 'disable unused functions' (that call is in the mode_changed branch at 766); also a successful return can mean the crtc was not in use or nothing changed (742-785). Real function at 550-814 (slice 505-770). Read in full; drm_crtc_helper_disable and drm_crtc_helper_set_mode internals not read.

name: drm_wait_vblank
prose: Precondition: dev and data (a union drm_wait_vblank) are valid; file_priv is used only on the event path. Returns -EINVAL without taking a vblank reference if dev->irq_enabled is not set, if the request type has _DRM_VBLANK_SIGNAL set, if it has bits outside the supported type/flags/high-crtc mask, or if the selected crtc (high-crtc field if nonzero, else 1 for _DRM_VBLANK_SECONDARY, else 0) is >= dev->num_crtcs. It then calls drm_vblank_get and returns its error if nonzero. With the reference held and the current count read, a relative request has seq added to the requested sequence; an absolute request is left; any other type value gives -EINVAL and goes to done. If _DRM_VBLANK_EVENT is set it returns drm_queue_vblank_event(dev, crtc, vblwait, file_priv) directly, without calling drm_vblank_put here, since the reference is kept for the event (what that function does on its failures was not read). Otherwise, with _DRM_VBLANK_NEXTONMISS and a requested sequence already passed it moves the request to seq + 1, records last_vblank_wait, then under vblank_time_lock sleeps with msleep (PCATCH, 3 second timeout) until the vblank count reaches the requested sequence or irq_enabled clears; a nonzero sleep result ends the wait and is returned negated (ERESTART becomes -ERESTARTSYS; a timeout gives -EWOULDBLOCK, a signal -EINTR). Unless the result is -EINTR it fills reply.sequence, reply.tval_sec and reply.tval_usec from drm_vblank_count_and_time. At done, on every non-event path after drm_vblank_get succeeded, it calls drm_vblank_put and returns ret (0 on a completed wait).
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the function itself validates irq_enabled, type bits and crtc and returns -EINVAL (drm_irq.c:1197-1220), so these are not preconditions. Original reviewer: event path does return without drm_vblank_put at 1244, and the timestamp is filled only in the non-event path; the old 'always released' claim is removed. Function at 1190-1300 (slice 1074-1325). Read in full; drm_queue_vblank_event not read.

name: ttm_bo_handle_move_mem
prose: Precondition: bo and mem are valid and the caller has bo reserved as the TTM code expects (not checked here). If either region is PCI-mapped or the old and new caching placements share no bit, it takes the old memory type manager's io lock (an error from that lock goes to out_err), unmaps the bo's virtual mappings and releases the lock. If the new memory type is not fixed it creates the bo->ttm if absent (ttm_bo_add_ttm), sets its caching with ttm_tt_set_placement_caching and, when the target is not TTM_PL_SYSTEM, binds it with ttm_tt_bind; any failure of these goes to out_err without any move_notify call. If bo currently lives in TTM_PL_SYSTEM it then calls the driver move_notify (if any), sets bo->mem = *mem, clears mem->mm_node and skips the move. Otherwise it calls move_notify (if any) and performs the move with ttm_bo_move_ttm when neither old nor new type is fixed, else with the driver move hook if present, else ttm_bo_move_memcpy. If the move fails and move_notify exists it calls move_notify again with the memory regions swapped around the call (bo->mem is the same value after the swap sequence), and goes to out_err. On success: if bo->evicted it calls invalidate_caches (a failure is only printed) and clears evicted; if bo->mem.mm_node is non-NULL it sets bo->offset from bo->mem.start and the manager's gpu_offset and bo->cur_placement from bo->mem.placement, else it sets only bo->offset to 0 and leaves cur_placement alone; it returns 0. At out_err it takes the memory type of the current bo->mem and, if that type is fixed and bo->ttm exists, unbinds and destroys the ttm and sets bo->ttm to NULL; it returns the error code. The io lock is released on all paths where it was taken.
note: Round 15 reviewer right: the lock, add_ttm, caching and bind failures jump to out_err (ttm_bo.c:424-451) without calling move_notify; only a failed move calls it (474-482). Original reviewer right: cur_placement is not updated when mm_node is NULL (495-500). The old claim that bo->mem is 'restored to its previous region' on failure was overstated: the swap at 476-481 leaves bo->mem with the value it had after the failed mover. Function at 410-513 (slice 261-511). Read in full; the move callees not read.

name: e1000_set_d0_lplu_state_82575
prose: Precondition: hw is a valid e1000_hw. If hw->phy.ops.read_reg is NULL it touches no register and returns E1000_SUCCESS. Otherwise it reads IGP02E1000_PHY_POWER_MGMT and returns that error if the read fails. If active is true it sets the D0_LPLU bit and writes the register back (returning the write error if any), then reads IGP01E1000_PHY_PORT_CONFIG, clears the SmartSpeed bit and writes it back; the status of that port-config read is overwritten by the write's status, so only the write error is returned in this branch (the cleared bit is written even if the read failed, using whatever data holds). If active is false it clears D0_LPLU and writes the power-management register; if phy->smart_speed is e1000_smart_speed_on or e1000_smart_speed_off, that write's status is overwritten by the next port-config read and a read or write failure there is returned after setting or clearing the SmartSpeed bit accordingly; for any other smart_speed value no further access is made and the status of the power-management write is returned. The function returns E1000_SUCCESS or the status described above.
note: Both reviewers right: in the active branch a failed port-config read is overwritten (e1000_82575.c:781-785), and in the inactive branch with smart_speed neither on nor off the power-management write failure IS returned (790-791, 798-825); the prose said it never propagates. Function at 758-829 (slice 535-804 cut head). Read in full; the PHY ops were not read.

name: e1000_update_nvm_checksum_ich8lan
prose: Precondition: hw is an initialised e1000_hw with NVM acquire, release and reload operations set. It first calls e1000_update_nvm_checksum_generic and returns its error if nonzero (that call may itself modify shadow RAM words). If nvm->type is not e1000_nvm_flash_sw it returns the generic call's result (0) without acquiring the NVM, committing to flash or resetting the shadow cache. Otherwise it calls nvm->ops.acquire (result ignored), detects the valid bank (a detection failure is not returned: bank 0 is assumed), erases the opposite flash bank (an erase error goes to release), then writes each of the E1000_SHADOW_RAM_WORDS words to the new bank byte by byte (a modified shadow word is used, otherwise the word is read from the old bank), with the signature word forced to have bits 15:14 set; a read or write error stops the loop. After a failed copy it releases the NVM and returns the error. After a successful copy it reads back the new bank's signature word and writes its high byte with bit 14 cleared, then writes 0 to the high byte of the old bank's signature word; an error in these steps goes to release. Only when everything succeeded does it clear every shadow_ram entry to unmodified and value 0xFFFF. It always calls nvm->ops.release on the flash path; if the result is zero it then calls nvm->ops.reload and waits 10 ms; on error the NVM is released but not reloaded and the shadow cache is left as it was. It returns the first nonzero status, logging it, or 0.
note: Both reviewers right: the non-flash_sw branch returns after the generic update at e1000_ich8lan.c:4256-4261 with no commit or cache reset, and that generic update may itself change shadow words. Real function at 4246-4386 (slice 4135-4387). Read in full; callees not read.

name: e1000_kmrn_lock_loss_workaround_ich8lan
prose: Precondition: hw is an initialised e1000_hw with ich8lan device-specific data. If dev_spec->kmrn_lock_loss_workaround_enabled is false it returns E1000_SUCCESS immediately without any hardware access. Otherwise it calls e1000_phy_has_link_generic(hw, 1, 0, &link) (which accesses the PHY; its return value is ignored) and returns E1000_SUCCESS if link is false. With link up it makes up to 10 attempts: each reads IGP3_KMRN_DIAG twice through phy.ops.read_reg, returning that read's error code if either read fails; if the second read has the PCS lock-loss bit clear it returns E1000_SUCCESS; otherwise it calls phy.ops.reset and waits 5 ms and tries again. If all 10 attempts show lock loss it sets E1000_PHY_CTRL_GBE_DISABLE and E1000_PHY_CTRL_NOND0A_GBE_DISABLE in E1000_PHY_CTRL, calls e1000_gig_downshift_workaround_ich8lan, and returns -E1000_ERR_PHY.
note: Round 15 reviewer right: when the workaround is enabled e1000_phy_has_link_generic is called (e1000_ich8lan.c:5513), so PHY registers can be touched before the link-down return; the old text said no PHY access. Original reviewer right: read_reg error returns at 5520-5525 (older prose now includes them). Function at 5496-5548 (slice 5421-5684 cut head). Read in full.

name: e1000_config_fc_after_link_up_generic
prose: Precondition: hw is an initialised e1000_hw with mac, phy and fc fields valid. First step: if mac->autoneg_failed is set and the media is fiber or internal serdes, or if it is clear and the media is copper, it calls e1000_force_mac_fc_generic and returns its error if nonzero (so for copper with autoneg_failed set, and for fiber/serdes without autoneg_failed, nothing is forced here). Copper with mac->autoneg: it reads PHY_STATUS twice (returning a read error if either fails); if MII_SR_AUTONEG_COMPLETE is clear it returns E1000_SUCCESS without changing hw->fc.current_mode (the MAC flow-control bits may already have been programmed by the first step); otherwise it reads the advertisement and link-partner registers (returning any read error), derives hw->fc.current_mode from the PAUSE/ASM_DIR bits (full or rx_pause if both PAUSE bits are set, depending on fc.requested_mode; tx_pause, rx_pause or none in the asymmetric cases), calls mac->ops.get_link_up_info (error returned) and forces current_mode to e1000_fc_none on half duplex, then calls e1000_force_mac_fc_generic (error returned). Internal serdes with mac->autoneg: it reads PCS_LSTAT; if auto-negotiation is not complete it returns E1000_SUCCESS without changing current_mode or the PCS/MAC bits; otherwise it derives current_mode from the PCS advertisement and link-partner registers the same way (without the half-duplex override), sets E1000_PCS_LCTL_FORCE_FCTRL in PCS_LCTL and calls e1000_force_mac_fc_generic (error returned). In all other cases it returns E1000_SUCCESS.
note: Both reviewers right: the copper incomplete-autoneg early return at e1000_mac.c:1403-1406 follows the force_mac_fc call made at 1377-1378 (copper with autoneg_failed clear), so the MAC bits may have been programmed; the serdes early return at 1542-1545 does leave PCS/MAC bits and current_mode untouched unless the first block forced them. Half-duplex override exists only in the copper branch (1517-1518). Real function at 1358-1655 (slice 1300-1555). Read in full.

name: e1000_check_for_serdes_link_generic
prose: Precondition: hw is an initialised e1000_hw with mac->txcw set. It reads CTRL, STATUS and RXCW. If the link-up status bit is clear and no /C/ is being received: on the first such observation (mac->autoneg_failed false) it sets mac->autoneg_failed to true and returns E1000_SUCCESS immediately without touching serdes_has_link; on later observations it clears the autoneg-enable bit in TXCW, sets SLU and full-duplex in CTRL and calls e1000_config_fc_after_link_up_generic, returning that call's error if nonzero. Otherwise, if CTRL has SLU set and /C/ is being received, it restores TXCW to mac->txcw, clears SLU in CTRL and sets mac->serdes_has_link true. Otherwise, if autoneg is currently disabled in TXCW (forced link), it waits 10 us and re-reads RXCW: with sync and no invalid codeword it sets serdes_has_link true, with no sync it sets it false, and with sync plus invalid codeword it leaves it unchanged. After that, if autoneg is enabled in TXCW it re-reads STATUS and, depending on the link-up bit and the RXCW sync and invalid-codeword bits after a 10 us wait, sets serdes_has_link true (up, synced, no invalid codeword) or false (any other combination). It returns E1000_SUCCESS at the end of those steps; the only other return value is the error from e1000_config_fc_after_link_up_generic.
note: Both reviewers right: the old 'always returns E1000_SUCCESS' ignores the return of the flow-control error at e1000_mac.c:885-889. Function at 848-945 (slice 789-1042). Read in full.

name: e1000_load_firmware
prose: Precondition: hw is an initialised e1000_hw and buffer holds at least length readable bytes. Returns -E1000_ERR_CONFIG if hw->mac.type is below e1000_i210 or if HICR lacks the host-enable or memory-base-enable bit; returns -E1000_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT if length is 0, not a multiple of 4, or above E1000_HI_FW_MAX_LENGTH. Otherwise it reads ICR_V2, sets the FW reset-enable and FW reset bits in HICR, and polls ICR_V2 up to 2 * E1000_HI_COMMAND_TIMEOUT times (1 ms apart) for E1000_ICR_MNG; it returns -E1000_ERR_HOST_INTERFACE_COMMAND if the loop index equals exactly E1000_HI_COMMAND_TIMEOUT afterwards (so the check is on that index value, not on the loop having run out). It then polls FWSM up to E1000_HI_COMMAND_TIMEOUT ms for FW valid with the host-interface-enable-only mode, returning -E1000_ERR_HOST_INTERFACE_COMMAND on timeout. It writes the buffer as 32-bit words into the host interface RAM, setting HIBBA at each block boundary, sets the E1000_HICR_C bit in HICR and polls up to E1000_HI_COMMAND_TIMEOUT ms for it to clear; if it does not clear it returns -E1000_ERR_HOST_INTERFACE_COMMAND, else E1000_SUCCESS. No locks are taken.
note: Slice 508-577 started mid-body; the real function is e1000_load_firmware (the old name e1000_load_firmware_82575 does not exist in the tree, grep of sys/dev/e1000 finds only e1000_load_firmware at e1000_manage.c:470-577). Old prose had the family check wrong (no 82575-specific check; code requires mac.type >= e1000_i210 at 476) and omitted the early -E1000_ERR_CONFIG and -E1000_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT returns. Read in full. The first-wait test 'i == E1000_HI_COMMAND_TIMEOUT' (517) is as in source even though the loop runs to twice that.

name: e1000_reset_hw_vf
prose: Precondition: hw and its mailbox ops (check_for_rst, write_posted, read_posted) are set up. It sets the reset bit in CTRL, then polls mbx->ops.check_for_rst(hw, 0) every 5 us until it reports a reset or E1000_VF_INIT_TIMEOUT iterations pass. If the poll ran out (timeout is 0) it returns the initial value -E1000_ERR_MAC_INIT with perm_addr unchanged. Otherwise it sets mbx->timeout to E1000_VF_MBX_INIT_TIMEOUT, posts a one-word E1000_VF_RESET message (the write_posted result is ignored), waits 10 ms, and calls read_posted for 3 words. If read_posted returns nonzero that error code is returned as is (not necessarily -E1000_ERR_MAC_INIT) and perm_addr is unchanged. If it succeeds and the first word equals E1000_VF_RESET | E1000_VT_MSGTYPE_ACK, the 6 bytes following that word are copied into hw->mac.perm_addr and 0 is returned; otherwise it returns -E1000_ERR_MAC_INIT without copying.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: ret_val is the read_posted result when it is nonzero (e1000_vf.c:288-295), not forced to -E1000_ERR_MAC_INIT. Original reviewer is wrong: when the poll times out ret_val keeps its initial -E1000_ERR_MAC_INIT (262, 278-298), so no success is returned. Function at 258-299 (slice 266-519). Read in full.

name: reset_system
prose: Precondition: none beyond type being an enum efi_reset value. Returns EINVAL if type is not EFI_RESET_COLD, EFI_RESET_WARM or EFI_RESET_SHUTDOWN. Returns ENXIO if the global efi_runtime is NULL. Otherwise it builds a zeroed efirt_callinfo for the "rt_reset" runtime service with four arguments (type, 0, 0, NULL) and the physical address of the runtime reset method, calls efi_call on it, and returns efi_call's return value unchanged. The function takes no locks itself.
note: Read in full at efirt.c:718-742. Behaviour of efi_call (locking, fault handling, return values) was not read, so the prose does not describe its result beyond passing it through. Slice 512-764 was only a window onto the function.
